# =============================================================================
# Immich Importer LXC - Photo Import & Cloud Backup
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 303 (existing)
# LAN IP: 192.168.1.223 | Container IP: 10.100.3.103
#
# Run immich-go for Google Photos import, rclone for B2 cloud backup.
# Non-Docker LXC with direct tool installation.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 303
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64
}

variable "swap" {
  type    = number
  default = 512
}

# Backblaze B2 credentials (from 1Password)
variable "b2_account_id" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "b2_application_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "rclone_crypt_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "rclone_crypt_password2" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# Immich configuration
variable "immich_server" {
  type    = string
  default = "http://192.168.1.222:2283"
}

variable "immich_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# Cloud backup schedule
variable "cloud_backup_schedule" {
  type    = string
  default = "0 3 * * 0,3"
}

# iCloud credentials (for icloudpd)
variable "icloud_username" {
  type        = string
  description = "Apple ID email for iCloud Photo download"
}

variable "icloud_password" {
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  description = "App-specific password for iCloud (generate at appleid.apple.com)"
}

# iCloud sync schedule (daily at 4 AM, after cloud backup)
variable "icloud_sync_schedule" {
  type    = string
  default = "0 4 * * *"
}

# iCloud download directory
variable "icloud_download_dir" {
  type    = string
  default = "/downloads/icloud"
}

# ntfy notification settings
variable "ntfy_server" {
  type    = string
  default = "https://ntfy.homelab.rambtech.dev"
}

variable "ntfy_topic" {
  type        = string
  default     = "icloud-sync"
  description = "ntfy topic for iCloud sync notifications"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Immich Importer Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Use LAN IP for SSH connections (existing container is on LAN network)
locals {
  ssh_host = local.lan_ips.immich_importer # 192.168.1.223
}

module "lxc" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-base"

  name         = "immich-importer"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (dual-NIC: container + LAN for internet access)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.photos.immich_importer}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.immich_importer}${local.network.lan_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Ubuntu template (matches existing container)
  template = "local:vztmpl/ubuntu-24.04-standard_24.04-2_amd64.tar.zst"
  os_type  = "ubuntu"

  # Container features
  unprivileged   = true
  enable_nesting = true
  enable_keyctl  = true

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key = local.ssh_public_key

  # Mount points for photos and imports
  mount_points = [
    {
      slot   = 0
      volume = "/tank/photos"
      path   = "/photos"
    },
    {
      slot   = 1
      volume = "/tank/cache/immich"
      path   = "/cache"
    },
    {
      slot   = 2
      volume = "/tank/importer"
      path   = "/importer"
    },
    {
      slot   = 3
      volume = "/tank/photo-import"
      path   = "/downloads"
    }
  ]

  # Proxmox Notes
  description = <<-EOT
# Immich Importer

Photo import (immich-go), iCloud sync (icloudpd), and cloud backup (rclone to B2)

## Services

- **icloudpd**: iCloud Photo Downloader
- **immich-go**: Photo importer to Immich
- **rclone**: Cloud backup to B2 (encrypted)

## Management

- SSH: `ssh root@${local.lan_ips.immich_importer}`

## iCloud Sync

**Schedule:** ${var.icloud_sync_schedule} (Daily 4 AM EST)

**First-time setup (requires 2FA):**
```bash
source /etc/profile.d/icloud-sync.sh
icloud-sync.sh auth
```

**Commands:**
```bash
icloud-sync.sh status    # Check sync status
icloud-sync.sh download  # Download from iCloud
icloud-sync.sh import    # Import to Immich
icloud-sync.sh sync      # Download + Import
```

**Logs:**
```bash
tail -f /var/log/icloud-sync.log
```

## Cloud Backup (B2)

**Schedule:** ${var.cloud_backup_schedule} (Wed and Sun 3 AM EST)

**Commands:**
```bash
cloud-sync.sh status     # Check B2 status
cloud-sync.sh photos     # Sync to B2
```

## Manual Import

**Run immich-go:**
```bash
immich-go -server ${var.immich_server} upload /downloads
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=immich-importer` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["immich-importer", "backup", "rclone", "icloud", "opentofu"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Wait for container to be ready
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "time_sleep" "wait_for_container" {
  depends_on      = [module.lxc]
  create_duration = "10s"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Install Dependencies (rclone, immich-go)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "null_resource" "install_dependencies" {
  depends_on = [time_sleep.wait_for_container]

  triggers = {
    container_id = var.container_id
  }

  connection {
    type        = "ssh"
    host        = local.ssh_host
    user        = "root"
    private_key = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
  }

  provisioner "remote-exec" {
    inline = [
      "export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive",
      "apt-get update -qq",
      "apt-get install -y -qq curl unzip cron python3",

      # Install uv (fast Python package manager)
      "if ! command -v uv &>/dev/null; then curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh; fi",
      "export PATH=\"$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH\"",

      # Install icloudpd (iCloud Photo Downloader) via uv
      "if ! command -v icloudpd &>/dev/null; then uv tool install icloudpd; fi",

      # Install rclone
      "if ! command -v rclone &>/dev/null; then curl -fsSL https://rclone.org/install.sh | bash; fi",

      # Install immich-go (latest release)
      "if ! command -v immich-go &>/dev/null; then",
      "  IMMICH_GO_VERSION=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/simulot/immich-go/releases/latest | grep tag_name | cut -d'\"' -f4)",
      "  curl -fsSL https://github.com/simulot/immich-go/releases/download/$${IMMICH_GO_VERSION}/immich-go_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz | tar -xzf - -C /usr/local/bin immich-go",
      "  chmod +x /usr/local/bin/immich-go",
      "fi",

      # Create directories
      "mkdir -p /root/.config/rclone",
      "mkdir -p /root/.icloudpd",
      "mkdir -p ${var.icloud_download_dir}",
      "mkdir -p /var/log",
    ]
  }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Local Config Files (generated from variables)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "local_sensitive_file" "rclone_conf" {
  filename = "${path.module}/.tmp/rclone.conf"
  content  = <<-CONF
[b2]
type = b2
account = ${var.b2_account_id}
key = ${var.b2_application_key}
hard_delete = true

[b2-crypt]
type = crypt
remote = b2:rambtech-homelab/photos-encrypted
password = ${var.rclone_crypt_password}
password2 = ${var.rclone_crypt_password2}
CONF
}

resource "local_sensitive_file" "icloud_env" {
  filename = "${path.module}/.tmp/icloud-env.sh"
  content  = <<-EOF
# iCloud sync environment variables
export ICLOUD_USERNAME="${var.icloud_username}"
export ICLOUD_DOWNLOAD_DIR="${var.icloud_download_dir}"
export IMMICH_SERVER="${var.immich_server}"
export IMMICH_API_KEY="${var.immich_api_key}"
export NTFY_SERVER="${var.ntfy_server}"
export NTFY_TOPIC="${var.ntfy_topic}"
EOF
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deploy Config Files via filesync
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "filesync_file" "rclone_conf" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.rclone_conf.filename
  destination = "/root/.config/rclone/rclone.conf"
  host        = local.ssh_host

  mode         = "0600"
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [null_resource.install_dependencies]
}

resource "filesync_file" "cloud_sync_script" {
  source      = "${path.module}/deploy/cloud-sync.sh"
  destination = "/usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh"
  host        = local.ssh_host

  mode         = "0755"
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [null_resource.install_dependencies]
}

resource "filesync_file" "icloud_sync_script" {
  source      = "${path.module}/deploy/icloud-sync.sh"
  destination = "/usr/local/bin/icloud-sync.sh"
  host        = local.ssh_host

  mode         = "0755"
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [null_resource.install_dependencies]
}

resource "filesync_file" "icloud_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.icloud_env.filename
  destination = "/etc/profile.d/icloud-sync.sh"
  host        = local.ssh_host

  mode         = "0644"
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [null_resource.install_dependencies]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configure Cron Jobs (Cloud Backup + iCloud Sync)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "null_resource" "configure_cron" {
  depends_on = [
    filesync_file.cloud_sync_script,
    filesync_file.icloud_sync_script,
    filesync_file.icloud_env,
    filesync_file.rclone_conf
  ]

  triggers = {
    container_id        = var.container_id
    cloud_schedule      = var.cloud_backup_schedule
    icloud_schedule     = var.icloud_sync_schedule
  }

  connection {
    type        = "ssh"
    host        = local.ssh_host
    user        = "root"
    private_key = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
  }

  provisioner "remote-exec" {
    inline = [
      # Clear existing cron entries for our scripts
      "crontab -l 2>/dev/null | grep -v 'cloud-sync.sh' | grep -v 'icloud-sync.sh' | crontab - || true",

      # Add cloud backup cron (B2 sync)
      "(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo '${var.cloud_backup_schedule} /usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh photos >> /var/log/cloud-sync-photos.log 2>&1') | crontab -",

      # Add iCloud sync cron (with environment variables)
      "(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo '${var.icloud_sync_schedule} . /etc/profile.d/icloud-sync.sh && /usr/local/bin/icloud-sync.sh sync >> /var/log/icloud-sync.log 2>&1') | crontab -",

      # Ensure cron service is running
      "systemctl enable cron",
      "systemctl start cron",

      "echo 'Cron configured:'",
      "echo '  Cloud backup: ${var.cloud_backup_schedule}'",
      "echo '  iCloud sync:  ${var.icloud_sync_schedule}'"
    ]
  }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.lxc.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = local.ssh_host
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = "ssh root@${local.ssh_host}"
}

output "cloud_backup_schedule" {
  value = var.cloud_backup_schedule
}

output "icloud_sync_schedule" {

# =============================================================================
# Immich Importer LXC - Photo Import & Cloud Backup
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 303 (existing)
# LAN IP: 192.168.1.223 | Container IP: 10.100.3.103
#
# Run immich-go for Google Photos import, rclone for B2 cloud backup.
# Non-Docker LXC with direct tool installation.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 303
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64
}

variable "swap" {
  type    = number
  default = 512
}

# Backblaze B2 credentials (from 1Password)
variable "b2_account_id" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "b2_application_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "rclone_crypt_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "rclone_crypt_password2" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# Immich configuration
variable "immich_server" {
  type    = string
  default = "http://192.168.1.222:2283"
}

variable "immich_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# Cloud backup schedule
variable "cloud_backup_schedule" {
  type    = string
  default = "0 3 * * 0,3"
}

# iCloud credentials (for icloudpd)
variable "icloud_username" {
  type        = string
  description = "Apple ID email for iCloud Photo download"
}

variable "icloud_password" {
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  description = "App-specific password for iCloud (generate at appleid.apple.com)"
}

# iCloud sync schedule (daily at 4 AM, after cloud backup)
variable "icloud_sync_schedule" {
  type    = string
  default = "0 4 * * *"
}

# iCloud download directory
variable "icloud_download_dir" {
  type    = string
  default = "/downloads/icloud"
}

# ntfy notification settings
variable "ntfy_server" {
  type    = string
  default = "https://ntfy.homelab.rambtech.dev"
}

variable "ntfy_topic" {
  type        = string
  default     = "icloud-sync"
  description = "ntfy topic for iCloud sync notifications"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Immich Importer Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Use LAN IP for SSH connections (existing container is on LAN network)
locals {
  ssh_host = local.lan_ips.immich_importer # 192.168.1.223
}

module "lxc" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-base"

  name         = "immich-importer"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (dual-NIC: container + LAN for internet access)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.photos.immich_importer}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.immich_importer}${local.network.lan_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Ubuntu template (matches existing container)
  template = "local:vztmpl/ubuntu-24.04-standard_24.04-2_amd64.tar.zst"
  os_type  = "ubuntu"

  # Container features
  unprivileged   = true
  enable_nesting = true
  enable_keyctl  = true

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key = local.ssh_public_key

  # Mount points for photos and imports
  mount_points = [
    {
      slot   = 0
      volume = "/tank/photos"
      path   = "/photos"
    },
    {
      slot   = 1
      volume = "/tank/cache/immich"
      path   = "/cache"
    },
    {
      slot   = 2
      volume = "/tank/importer"
      path   = "/importer"
    },
    {
      slot   = 3
      volume = "/tank/photo-import"
      path   = "/downloads"
    }
  ]

  # Proxmox Notes
  description = <<-EOT
# Immich Importer

Photo import (immich-go), iCloud sync (icloudpd), and cloud backup (rclone to B2)

## Services

- **icloudpd**: iCloud Photo Downloader
- **immich-go**: Photo importer to Immich
- **rclone**: Cloud backup to B2 (encrypted)

## Management

- SSH: `ssh root@${local.lan_ips.immich_importer}`

## iCloud Sync

**Schedule:** ${var.icloud_sync_schedule} (Daily 4 AM EST)

**First-time setup (requires 2FA):**
```bash
source /etc/profile.d/icloud-sync.sh
icloud-sync.sh auth
```

**Commands:**
```bash
icloud-sync.sh status    # Check sync status
icloud-sync.sh download  # Download from iCloud
icloud-sync.sh import    # Import to Immich
icloud-sync.sh sync      # Download + Import
```

**Logs:**
```bash
tail -f /var/log/icloud-sync.log
```

## Cloud Backup (B2)

**Schedule:** ${var.cloud_backup_schedule} (Wed and Sun 3 AM EST)

**Commands:**
```bash
cloud-sync.sh status     # Check B2 status
cloud-sync.sh photos     # Sync to B2
```

## Manual Import

**Run immich-go:**
```bash
immich-go -server ${var.immich_server} upload /downloads
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=immich-importer` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["immich-importer", "backup", "rclone", "icloud", "opentofu"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Wait for container to be ready
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "time_sleep" "wait_for_container" {
  depends_on      = [module.lxc]
  create_duration = "10s"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Install Dependencies (rclone, immich-go)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "null_resource" "install_dependencies" {
  depends_on = [time_sleep.wait_for_container]

  triggers = {
    container_id = var.container_id
  }

  connection {
    type        = "ssh"
    host        = local.ssh_host
    user        = "root"
    private_key = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
  }

  provisioner "remote-exec" {
    inline = [
      "export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive",
      "apt-get update -qq",
      "apt-get install -y -qq curl unzip cron python3",

      # Install uv (fast Python package manager)
      "if ! command -v uv &>/dev/null; then curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh; fi",
      "export PATH=\"$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH\"",

      # Install icloudpd (iCloud Photo Downloader) via uv
      "if ! command -v icloudpd &>/dev/null; then uv tool install icloudpd; fi",

      # Install rclone
      "if ! command -v rclone &>/dev/null; then curl -fsSL https://rclone.org/install.sh | bash; fi",

      # Install immich-go (latest release)
      "if ! command -v immich-go &>/dev/null; then",
      "  IMMICH_GO_VERSION=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/simulot/immich-go/releases/latest | grep tag_name | cut -d'\"' -f4)",
      "  curl -fsSL https://github.com/simulot/immich-go/releases/download/$${IMMICH_GO_VERSION}/immich-go_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz | tar -xzf - -C /usr/local/bin immich-go",
      "  chmod +x /usr/local/bin/immich-go",
      "fi",

      # Create directories
      "mkdir -p /root/.config/rclone",
      "mkdir -p /root/.icloudpd",
      "mkdir -p ${var.icloud_download_dir}",
      "mkdir -p /var/log",
    ]
  }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Local Config Files (generated from variables)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "local_sensitive_file" "rclone_conf" {
  filename = "${path.module}/.tmp/rclone.conf"
  content  = <<-CONF
[b2]
type = b2
account = ${var.b2_account_id}
key = ${var.b2_application_key}
hard_delete = true

[b2-crypt]
type = crypt
remote = b2:rambtech-homelab/photos-encrypted
password = ${var.rclone_crypt_password}
password2 = ${var.rclone_crypt_password2}
CONF
}

resource "local_sensitive_file" "icloud_env" {
  filename = "${path.module}/.tmp/icloud-env.sh"
  content  = <<-EOF
# iCloud sync environment variables
export ICLOUD_USERNAME="${var.icloud_username}"
export ICLOUD_DOWNLOAD_DIR="${var.icloud_download_dir}"
export IMMICH_SERVER="${var.immich_server}"
export IMMICH_API_KEY="${var.immich_api_key}"
export NTFY_SERVER="${var.ntfy_server}"
export NTFY_TOPIC="${var.ntfy_topic}"
EOF
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Deploy Config Files via filesync
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "filesync_file" "rclone_conf" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.rclone_conf.filename
  destination = "/root/.config/rclone/rclone.conf"
  host        = local.ssh_host

  mode         = "0600"
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [null_resource.install_dependencies]
}

resource "filesync_file" "cloud_sync_script" {
  source      = "${path.module}/deploy/cloud-sync.sh"
  destination = "/usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh"
  host        = local.ssh_host

  mode         = "0755"
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [null_resource.install_dependencies]
}

resource "filesync_file" "icloud_sync_script" {
  source      = "${path.module}/deploy/icloud-sync.sh"
  destination = "/usr/local/bin/icloud-sync.sh"
  host        = local.ssh_host

  mode         = "0755"
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [null_resource.install_dependencies]
}

resource "filesync_file" "icloud_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.icloud_env.filename
  destination = "/etc/profile.d/icloud-sync.sh"
  host        = local.ssh_host

  mode         = "0644"
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [null_resource.install_dependencies]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configure Cron Jobs (Cloud Backup + iCloud Sync)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "null_resource" "configure_cron" {
  depends_on = [
    filesync_file.cloud_sync_script,
    filesync_file.icloud_sync_script,
    filesync_file.icloud_env,
    filesync_file.rclone_conf
  ]

  triggers = {
    container_id        = var.container_id
    cloud_schedule      = var.cloud_backup_schedule
    icloud_schedule     = var.icloud_sync_schedule
  }

  connection {
    type        = "ssh"
    host        = local.ssh_host
    user        = "root"
    private_key = file(var.ssh_private_key_path)
  }

  provisioner "remote-exec" {
    inline = [
      # Clear existing cron entries for our scripts
      "crontab -l 2>/dev/null | grep -v 'cloud-sync.sh' | grep -v 'icloud-sync.sh' | crontab - || true",

      # Add cloud backup cron (B2 sync)
      "(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo '${var.cloud_backup_schedule} /usr/local/bin/cloud-sync.sh photos >> /var/log/cloud-sync-photos.log 2>&1') | crontab -",

      # Add iCloud sync cron (with environment variables) - sync-albums downloads all albums + imports
      "(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo '${var.icloud_sync_schedule} . /etc/profile.d/icloud-sync.sh && /usr/local/bin/icloud-sync.sh sync-albums >> /var/log/icloud-sync.log 2>&1') | crontab -",

      # Ensure cron service is running
      "systemctl enable cron",
      "systemctl start cron",

      "echo 'Cron configured:'",
      "echo '  Cloud backup: ${var.cloud_backup_schedule}'",
      "echo '  iCloud sync:  ${var.icloud_sync_schedule}'"
    ]
  }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.lxc.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = local.ssh_host
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = "ssh root@${local.ssh_host}"
}

output "cloud_backup_schedule" {
  value = var.cloud_backup_schedule
}

output "icloud_sync_schedule" {
  value = var.icloud_sync_schedule
}

# Prometheus Configuration
# Receives metrics from OpenTelemetry Collector and scrapes additional targets

global:
  scrape_interval: 30s
  evaluation_interval: 30s
  external_labels:
    monitor: 'homelab'

# Alerting configuration
alerting:
  alertmanagers:
    - static_configs:

# =============================================================================
# Monitoring LXC - OpenTelemetry + Prometheus + Grafana + Uptime Kuma + ntfy
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 500
# IP: 192.168.1.229
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Observability stack for metrics, dashboards, and alerting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 500
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "monitoring"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "tank"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Privileged for Docker
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Monitoring"
  service_description = "OpenTelemetry-based monitoring stack with Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting"

  service_urls = {
    grafana      = "https://grafana.${var.domain_internal}"
    prometheus   = "https://prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"
    alertmanager = "https://alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"
    uptime_kuma  = "https://status.${var.domain_internal}"
    ntfy         = "https://ntfy.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct_otel_grpc = "http://192.168.1.229:4317"

# OpenTofu IaC Commands
# https://taskfile.dev
#
# Each app has its own state file in tofu/apps/<app>/
# Use APP=dashboards|openwebui|portainer|etc to specify which app

version: '3'

vars:
  TOFU_DIR: "tofu"

tasks:
  tofu:init:
    desc: "Initialize OpenTofu for an app (APP=dashboards|openwebui|portainer)"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu init
    requires:
      vars: [APP]

  tofu:plan:
    desc: "Plan infrastructure changes for an app"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - pwd
      - tofu plan -out=tfplan
    requires:
      vars: [APP]
    preconditions:
      - sh: test -d .terraform
        msg: "Run 'task tofu:init APP={{.APP}}' first"

  tofu:apply:
    desc: "Apply planned infrastructure changes for an app (optional: REPLACE='resource.name')"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu apply {{if .REPLACE}}-replace='{{.REPLACE}}'{{else}}tfplan{{end}} 
    requires:
      vars: [APP]
    preconditions:
      - sh: '{{if .REPLACE}}true{{else}}test -f tfplan{{end}}'
        msg: "Run 'task tofu:plan APP={{.APP}}' first"

  tofu:destroy:
    desc: "Destroy an app's infrastructure"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - echo "⚠️  This will destroy {{.APP}} infrastructure!"
      - tofu destroy
    requires:
      vars: [APP]
    prompt: "Are you sure you want to destroy {{.APP}}?"

  tofu:output:
    desc: "Show infrastructure outputs for an app"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu output
    requires:
      vars: [APP]

  tofu:state:
    desc: "List all resources in an app's state"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu state list
    requires:
      vars: [APP]

  tofu:state:rm:
    desc: "Remove a resource from state (APP, RESOURCE)"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu state rm '{{.RESOURCE}}'
    requires:
      vars: [APP, RESOURCE]

  tofu:import:
    desc: "Import existing resource into state (APP, ADDR, ID)"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu import '{{.ADDR}}' '{{.ID}}'
    requires:
      vars: [APP, ADDR, ID]

  tofu:show:
    desc: "Show saved plan details for an app"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu show tfplan
    requires:
      vars: [APP]
    preconditions:
      - sh: test -f tfplan
        msg: "Run 'task tofu:plan APP={{.APP}}' first"

  tofu:fmt:
    desc: "Format all Terraform files"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu fmt -recursive

  tofu:validate:
    desc: "Validate an app's configuration"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu validate
    requires:
      vars: [APP]

  tofu:encryption:setup:
    desc: "Set up state encryption passphrase in 1Password"
    cmds:
      - |
        echo "Creating 1Password item for state encryption..."
        PASSPHRASE=$(openssl rand -base64 32)
        op item create \
          --category=password \
          --title="opentofu" \
          --vault="homelab" \
          "password=$PASSPHRASE" \
          "notes=OpenTofu state encryption passphrase for homelab IaC"
        echo "✅ Created 1Password item 'opentofu'"
        echo "The passphrase will be automatically retrieved when running tofu commands"

  tofu:encryption:test:
    desc: "Test state encryption passphrase retrieval"
    cmds:
      - |
        if [ -n "$TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase" ]; then
          echo "✅ State encryption passphrase is set (${#TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase} chars)"
        else
          echo "❌ State encryption passphrase not set"
          echo "Run 'task tofu:encryption:setup' or set TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase"
          exit 1
        fi

  tofu:ssh:
    desc: "SSH to a deployed LXC by app name"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/tofu/ssh.sh {{.APP}}
    requires:
      vars: [APP]

  tofu:logs:
    desc: "View Docker logs from a deployed app"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/tofu/logs.sh {{.APP}} {{.SERVICE}}
    requires:
      vars: [APP, SERVICE]

  tofu:info:
    desc: "Show OpenTofu IaC status"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/tofu/info.sh

# Prometheus Configuration
# Receives metrics from OpenTelemetry Collector and scrapes additional targets

global:
  scrape_interval: 30s
  evaluation_interval: 30s
  external_labels:
    monitor: 'homelab'

# Alerting configuration
alerting:
  alertmanagers:
    - static_configs:
        - targets:
            - alertmanager:9093

# Rule files for alerts
rule_files:
  - /etc/prometheus/alerts/*.yml

# Scrape configurations
scrape_configs:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Monitoring Stack Self-Monitoring
  # ==========================================================================

  # Prometheus self-monitoring
  - job_name: 'prometheus'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['localhost:9090']

  # OpenTelemetry Collector metrics
  - job_name: 'otel-collector'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['otel-collector:8888']

  # Alertmanager metrics
  - job_name: 'alertmanager'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['alertmanager:9093']

  # Grafana metrics
  - job_name: 'grafana'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['grafana:3000']

  # ==========================================================================
  # Traefik Reverse Proxy Metrics
  # ==========================================================================
  - job_name: 'traefik'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['10.100.2.200:8082']
        labels:
          instance: 'traefik'
          lxc_id: '200'

  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer Agents - Container Management Metrics (HTTPS required)
  # Note: Portainer agents require HTTPS - uncomment and configure if needed
  # ==========================================================================
  - job_name: 'portainer-agent'
    scheme: https
    tls_config:
      insecure_skip_verify: true
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['10.100.1.100:9001']
        labels:
          instance: 'portainer-agent'
          lxc_id: '100'

  # ==========================================================================
  # cAdvisor - Docker Container Metrics
  # Deploy cAdvisor to each Docker host to enable container metrics
  # ==========================================================================
  # - job_name: 'cadvisor'
  #   static_configs:
  #     - targets:
  #         - '192.168.1.157:8081'  # portainer
  #         - '192.168.1.196:8081'  # network-services

# Remote write receiver enabled via --web.enable-remote-write-receiver flag
# This allows OTEL collector to push metrics

whats the best way to approach this? do we use these static configs or do we use like a prometheus agent?

Good question. Here are the main approaches:

**1. Static configs (current approach)**
- Simple, works for small setups
- Requires manual IP updates when things change
- Each service needs native Prometheus metrics or an exporter

**2. Prometheus exporters (sidecars)**
- Deploy exporters alongside services (e.g., `adguard-exporter`, `immich-exporter`)
- More metrics, but more containers to manage

**3. OpenTelemetry Collector (you already have this!)**
- OTEL collector at `10.100.5.100:4317/4318` is already running
- Services push metrics to OTEL → OTEL pushes to Prometheus
- More modern, push-based, no firewall issues
- Services need OTEL SDK or agent

**4. Service discovery**
- Consul, DNS-SD, or file-based discovery
- Overkill for homelab size

**My recommendation for your setup:**

Since you already have **OTEL Collector** running, the cleanest approach is:

1. **Traefik** → Keep static (already working, has native Prometheus)
2. **AdGuard** → Enable built-in Prometheus metrics (just a checkbox)
3. **Immich** → Has native OTEL support, configure it to push to your collector
4. **Jellyfin** → Use static config + Prometheus plugin (no OTEL support)

This gives you a hybrid approach - OTEL where supported, static scrapes for legacy apps.

# Immich - Self-hosted photo and video management
# https://immich.app/docs/install/docker-compose
# Updated: 2025-12 based on official v1.123+ config

name: immich

services:
  immich-server:
    container_name: immich_server
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release}
    # Hardware transcoding: VAAPI for AMD GPU
    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    group_add:
      - video
    volumes:
      - ${UPLOAD_LOCATION}:/usr/src/app/upload
      - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
    env_file:
      - .env
    ports:
      - 2283:2283
    depends_on:
      - redis
      - database
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      disable: false

  immich-machine-learning:
    container_name: immich_machine_learning
    # Using CPU image since AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150) needs ROCm 6.4.4+
    # Immich ROCm image only has 6.3.4
    # Change to :release-rocm if/when Immich updates ROCm version
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-machine-learning:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release}
    # Uncomment below and change image tag to :release-rocm when ROCm 6.4.4+ is available
    # devices:
    #   - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    #   - /dev/kfd:/dev/kfd
    # group_add:
    #   - video
    #   - render
    volumes:
      - model-cache:/cache
    env_file:
      - .env
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      disable: false

  redis:
    container_name: immich_redis
    image: docker.io/valkey/valkey:8-bookworm
    healthcheck:
      test: valkey-cli ping || exit 1
    restart: unless-stopped

  database:
    container_name: immich_postgres
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres:14-vectorchord0.4.3-pgvectors0.2.0
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USERNAME}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_DATABASE_NAME}
      POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: '--data-checksums'
    volumes:
      - ${DB_DATA_LOCATION}:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: >-
        pg_isready --dbname="$${POSTGRES_DB}" --username="$${POSTGRES_USER}" || exit
        1; Chksum="$$(psql --dbname="$${POSTGRES_DB}" --username="$${POSTGRES_USER}"
        --tuples-only --no-align --command='SELECT COALESCE(SUM(googlechecksum(googlechecksum(tableoid,
        entity_id))), 0) FROM entity WHERE NOT is_external')"; Prev="$$(cat
        /tmp/.immich_db_checksum 2>/dev/null || echo '')"; echo "$${Chksum}" >
        /tmp/.immich_db_checksum; test "$${Prev}" = '' -o "$${Prev}" = "$${Chksum}"
      interval: 5m
      start_interval: 30s
      start_period: 5m
    command:
      [
        'postgres',
        '-c',
        'shared_preload_libraries=vchord.so,vectors.so',
        '-c',
        'search_path="$$user", public, vectors',
        '-c',
        'logging_collector=on',
        '-c',
        'max_wal_size=2GB',
        '-c',
        'shared_buffers=512MB',
        '-c',
        'wal_compression=on',
      ]
    restart: unless-stopped

  # Portainer Agent for remote management
  portainer-agent:
    container_name: portainer_agent
    image: portainer/agent:latest
    ports:
      - 9001:9001
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  model-cache:

    # Uncomment below and change image tag to :release-rocm when ROCm 6.4.4+ is available
    # devices:
    #   - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    #   - /dev/kfd:/dev/kfd
    # group_add:
    #   - video
    #   - render
    volumes:
      - model-cache:/cache
    env_file:
      - .env
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      disable: false

  redis:
    container_name: immich_redis
    image: docker.io/valkey/valkey:8-bookworm
    healthcheck:
      test: valkey-cli ping || exit 1
    restart: unless-stopped

  database:
    container_name: immich_postgres
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres:14-vectorchord0.4.3-pgvectors0.2.0
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USERNAME}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_DATABASE_NAME}
      POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: '--data-checksums'
    volumes:
      - ${DB_DATA_LOCATION}:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: >-
        pg_isready --dbname="$${POSTGRES_DB}" --username="$${POSTGRES_USER}" || exit
        1; Chksum="$$(psql --dbname="$${POSTGRES_DB}" --username="$${POSTGRES_USER}"
        --tuples-only --no-align --command='SELECT COALESCE(SUM(googlechecksum(googlechecksum(tableoid,
        entity_id))), 0) FROM entity WHERE NOT is_external')"; Prev="$$(cat
        /tmp/.immich_db_checksum 2>/dev/null || echo '')"; echo "$${Chksum}" >
        /tmp/.immich_db_checksum; test "$${Prev}" = '' -o "$${Prev}" = "$${Chksum}"
      interval: 5m
      start_interval: 30s
      start_period: 5m
    command:
      [
        'postgres',
        '-c',
        'shared_preload_libraries=vchord.so,vectors.so',
        '-c',
        'search_path="$$user", public, vectors',
        '-c',
        'logging_collector=on',
        '-c',
        'max_wal_size=2GB',
        '-c',
        'shared_buffers=512MB',
        '-c',
        'wal_compression=on',
      ]
    restart: unless-stopped

  # Portainer Agent for remote management
  portainer-agent:
    container_name: portainer_agent
    image: portainer/agent:latest
    ports:
      - 9001:9001
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
    restart: unless-stopped

# Immich - Self-hosted photo and video management
# https://immich.app/docs/install/docker-compose
# Updated: 2025-12 based on official v1.123+ config

name: immich

services:
  immich-server:
    container_name: immich_server
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release}
    # Hardware transcoding: VAAPI for AMD GPU
    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    group_add:
      - video
    volumes:
      - ${UPLOAD_LOCATION}:/usr/src/app/upload
      - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro
    env_file:
      - .env
    ports:
      - 2283:2283
    depends_on:
      - redis
      - database
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      disable: false

  immich-machine-learning:
    container_name: immich_machine_learning
    # Using CPU image since AMD Radeon 890M (gfx1150) needs ROCm 6.4.4+
    # Immich ROCm image only has 6.3.4
    # Change to :release-rocm if/when Immich updates ROCm version
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-machine-learning:${IMMICH_VERSION:-release}
    # Uncomment below and change image tag to :release-rocm when ROCm 6.4.4+ is available
    # devices:
    #   - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    #   - /dev/kfd:/dev/kfd
    # group_add:
    #   - video
    #   - render
    volumes:
      - model-cache:/cache
    env_file:
      - .env
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      disable: false

  redis:
    container_name: immich_redis
    image: docker.io/valkey/valkey:8-bookworm
    healthcheck:
      test: valkey-cli ping || exit 1
    restart: unless-stopped

  database:
    container_name: immich_postgres
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres:14-vectorchord0.4.3-pgvectors0.2.0
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USERNAME}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_DATABASE_NAME}
      POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: '--data-checksums'
    volumes:
      - ${DB_DATA_LOCATION}:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: >-
        pg_isready --dbname="$${POSTGRES_DB}" --username="$${POSTGRES_USER}" || exit
        1; Chksum="$$(psql --dbname="$${POSTGRES_DB}" --username="$${POSTGRES_USER}"
        --tuples-only --no-align --command='SELECT COALESCE(SUM(googlechecksum(googlechecksum(tableoid,
        entity_id))), 0) FROM entity WHERE NOT is_external')"; Prev="$$(cat
        /tmp/.immich_db_checksum 2>/dev/null || echo '')"; echo "$${Chksum}" >
        /tmp/.immich_db_checksum; test "$${Prev}" = '' -o "$${Prev}" = "$${Chksum}"
      interval: 5m
      start_interval: 30s
      start_period: 5m
    command:
      [
        'postgres',
        '-c',
        'shared_preload_libraries=vchord.so,vectors.so',
        '-c',
        'search_path="$$user", public, vectors',
        '-c',
        'logging_collector=on',
        '-c',
        'max_wal_size=2GB',
        '-c',
        'shared_buffers=512MB',
        '-c',
        'wal_compression=on',
      ]
    restart: unless-stopped

  # Portainer Agent for remote management
  portainer-agent:
    container_name: portainer_agent
    image: portainer/agent:latest
    ports:
      - 9001:9001
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  model-cache:

## Native Prometheus Support (New in 2025)

A recent pull request (PR #7937) implements native Prometheus metrics support for AdGuard Home, addressing the long-standing community request for built-in monitoring capabilities.(no content)The native implementation exposes metrics endpoint at `/metrics` (without auth, similar to /dns-query).

### Native Metrics Exposed:
The native metrics include:
- `adguard_dns_queries_total{result}` - Total DNS queries by processing result
- `adguard_dns_response_time_seconds{result}` - DNS response time histograms
- Standard Go metrics (memory, goroutines, GC, etc.)(no content)Note that the metrics endpoint is unauthenticated like the `/dns-query` endpoint for Prometheus scraping.

## Third-Party Exporters (Current Alternative)

If you're using an older version of AdGuard Home without native Prometheus support, there are several third-party exporters available:

1. **adguard-exporter by henrywhitaker3** - This is a Prometheus exporter for AdGuard Home that runs on port 9618 by default.

2. **adguardexporter by znand-dev** - A lightweight Prometheus exporter written in Go that exposes detailed metrics from your AdGuard Home instance — including DNS statistics, blocked domains, upstreams, and client data.

3. **adguard-exporter by ebrianne** - Runs on port 9617 and can be configured via Docker.

**Summary**: The native `/metrics` endpoint is coming to AdGuard Home (PR #7937 from July 2025). Until then, you'll need to use a third-party exporter which typically exposes metrics on ports like 9617 or 9618.

can you tell me whats. the plugin for jellyfin?

The Jellyfin Prometheus metrics plugin is called **"Prometheus Metrics"** (or sometimes "Prometheus Exporter").

To install it:
1. Go to Jellyfin **Dashboard** → **Plugins** → **Catalog**
2. Search for "Prometheus" 
3. Install **"Prometheus Metrics"** plugin
4. Restart Jellyfin

After installation, metrics are exposed at `http://<jellyfin-ip>:8096/metrics`.

You can also install via the [Jellyfin Plugin Repositories](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-plugin-prometheus) if it's not in the default catalog.

Once installed, uncomment the jellyfin job in prometheus.yml and deploy.
I dont see it in my jellyfinplugin search

The Prometheus plugin might not be in the default Jellyfin catalog. You may need to add a third-party repository or use an external exporter instead.

**Options:**

1. **External exporter** - [jellyfin-exporter](https://github.com/dr1s/jellyfin_exporter) runs as a separate container and scrapes the Jellyfin API

2. **Add third-party repo** - Some plugins are in community repos that need to be added manually in Jellyfin settings

3. **Skip Jellyfin metrics for now** - Jellyfin doesn't have great native Prometheus support

The external exporter approach is probably most reliable. Would you like me to add jellyfin-exporter as a sidecar to the Jellyfin docker-compose?

# Homelab Alert Rules
# Only includes alerts for metrics we actually collect

groups:
  - name: services
    interval: 1m
    rules:
      # Prometheus target down
      - alert: TargetDown
        expr: up == 0
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: critical
        annotations:
          summary: "Target {{ $labels.instance }} is down"
          description: "Prometheus cannot reach {{ $labels.job }} target {{ $labels.instance }}"

      # Traefik high error rate
      - alert: TraefikHighErrorRate
        expr: sum(rate(traefik_entrypoint_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(traefik_entrypoint_requests_total[5m])) > 0.05
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "High error rate on Traefik"
          description: "More than 5% of requests are returning 5xx errors"

      # Traefik backend down
      - alert: TraefikBackendDown
        expr: traefik_service_server_up == 0
        for: 2m
        labels:
          severity: critical
        annotations:
          summary: "Traefik backend {{ $labels.service }} is down"
          description: "Backend service {{ $labels.service }} is not responding"

  - name: proxmox
    interval: 1m
    rules:
      # Proxmox host high CPU
      - alert: ProxmoxHighCPU
        expr: proxmox_node_cpustat_cpu_percent > 80
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "High CPU on Proxmox node"
          description: "Proxmox node CPU usage above 80% for 10 minutes (current: {{ $value | printf \"%.1f\" }}%)"

      # Proxmox host memory high
      - alert: ProxmoxHighMemory
        expr: (proxmox_node_memory_memused_bytes / proxmox_node_memory_memtotal_bytes) * 100 > 85
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "High memory on Proxmox node"
          description: "Proxmox node memory usage above 85% for 10 minutes"

      # Proxmox storage low
      - alert: ProxmoxStorageLow
        expr: (proxmox_storage_used_bytes / proxmox_storage_total_bytes) * 100 > 85
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "Low storage on {{ $labels.storage }}"
          description: "Proxmox storage {{ $labels.storage }} is above 85% used"

      # Proxmox storage critical
      - alert: ProxmoxStorageCritical
        expr: (proxmox_storage_used_bytes / proxmox_storage_total_bytes) * 100 > 95
        for: 2m
        labels:
          severity: critical
        annotations:
          summary: "Critical storage on {{ $labels.storage }}"
          description: "Proxmox storage {{ $labels.storage }} is above 95% used"

      # LXC/VM down (no metrics for 5 minutes)
      - alert: ProxmoxVMDown
        expr: changes(proxmox_vm_uptime_seconds[5m]) == 0 and proxmox_vm_uptime_seconds > 0
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "VM/LXC {{ $labels.name }} may be unresponsive"
          description: "No uptime changes detected for VM/LXC {{ $labels.vmid }} ({{ $labels.name }})"

  - name: monitoring
    interval: 1m
    rules:
      # Alertmanager not receiving alerts
      - alert: AlertmanagerNotReceiving
        expr: rate(alertmanager_alerts_received_total[5m]) == 0
        for: 15m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "Alertmanager not receiving alerts"
          description: "Alertmanager has not received any alerts in 15 minutes"

      # Prometheus TSDB high cardinality
      - alert: PrometheusTSDBHighCardinality
        expr: prometheus_tsdb_head_series > 100000
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "Prometheus high time series count"
          description: "Prometheus has more than 100k active time series (current: {{ $value }})"

content.text:
Yes, this is a self-referential alert - it fires when no alerts are received, which then sends an alert, which resolves it. It's a bit of a paradox.

**Options:**
1. **Increase the `for` duration** - e.g., 30m or 1h instead of 15m
2. **Remove the alert entirely** - it's not very useful since it self-resolves
3. **Change the logic** - check if Alertmanager is unhealthy instead of checking for alerts

I'd recommend option 2 (remove it) since a healthy quiet system shouldn't trigger alerts. But if you want to keep some monitoring, let me increase it to 1h:

content.text: Done. The `AlertmanagerNotReceiving` alert has been removed. No more noisy self-referential alerts.

so my biggest concern with our observability is that we dont have healthchecks built into the system anywhere that can alert us. while metrics are excellent to get whenever available, the bigger concern is making sure that we have our services up and running without any issues. And if any of our services goes down, we can be alerted

You're right - metrics are nice, but **uptime monitoring and health checks** are critical for knowing when things break.

You already have **Uptime Kuma** running at `status.homelab.rambtech.dev` - that's the best tool for this in your stack.

**Uptime Kuma can:**
- HTTP/HTTPS health checks for all your services
- TCP port checks

Uptime Kuma uses SQLite (`kuma.db`) for storage, not config files. This makes declarative config harder, but there's a solution: **[Uptime Kuma API](https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/wiki/API)** or **[kuma-cli](https://github.com/lucasctrl/kuma-cli)**.

However, there's a better approach for IaC: **[Autokuma](https://github.com/BigBoot/AutoKuma)** - a sidecar that manages Uptime Kuma monitors from Docker labels or config files.

Let me add AutoKuma to the monitoring stack:

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # OpenTelemetry Collector - Central telemetry receiver and router
  # ==========================================================================
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:latest
    container_name: otel-collector
    command: ["--config=/etc/otelcol/config.yaml"]
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # OTLP gRPC receiver
      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP receiver
      - "8888:8888"   # Prometheus metrics (collector self-metrics)
      - "8889:8889"   # Prometheus exporter (for scraped metrics)
    volumes:
      - ./otel-collector/config.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml:ro
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prometheus - Metrics storage and alerting
  # ==========================================================================
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:latest
    container_name: prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d'
      - '--web.enable-lifecycle'
      - '--web.enable-remote-write-receiver'
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./prometheus/alerts:/etc/prometheus/alerts:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Alertmanager - Alert routing and notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:latest
    container_name: alertmanager
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml'
      - '--storage.path=/alertmanager'
    ports:
      - "9093:9093"
    volumes:
      - ./alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:ro
      - ./alertmanager/templates:/etc/alertmanager/templates:ro
      - alertmanager_data:/alertmanager
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana - Visualization and dashboards
  # ==========================================================================
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:latest
    container_name: grafana
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Uptime Kuma - HTTP endpoint monitoring and status page
  # ==========================================================================
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:latest
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"
    volumes:
      - uptime_kuma_data:/app/data
    dns:
      - 192.168.1.196  # AdGuard DNS for local domain resolution
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy - Push notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:latest
    container_name: ntfy
    command:
      - serve
      - --cache-file=/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
      - --attachment-cache-dir=/var/cache/ntfy/attachments
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ntfy_cache:/var/cache/ntfy
      - ntfy_data:/var/lib/ntfy
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer Agent - Container management
  # ==========================================================================
  portainer-agent:
    image: portainer/agent:latest
    container_name: portainer-agent
    ports:
      - "9001:9001"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

volumes:
  prometheus_data:
  alertmanager_data:
  grafana_data:
  uptime_kuma_data:
  ntfy_cache:
  ntfy_data:

content.content:
# Static Monitors JSON Format in AutoKuma

Based on the documentation provided, AutoKuma supports static monitors through JSON files, but the exact JSON structure isn't explicitly detailed in the README.

## Key Information

The documentation states: **"To create static Monitors just add a .json or .toml file in the directory specified by `AUTOKUMA__STATIC_MONITORS`"**

## Where to Find Examples

The README directs users to examine working examples: **"take a look at [the examples here](/BigBoot/AutoKuma/blob/master/monitors)."**

These example files in the `/monitors` directory would demonstrate the proper JSON structure and field requirements.

## Important Details

- Static monitors use the **filename (without extension) as the monitor ID**
- The default directory for static monitors varies by platform (Linux: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autokuma/static-monitors/`, macOS: `$HOME/Library/Application Support/autokuma/static-monitors/`, Windows: `%LocalAppData%\autokuma\static-monitors\`)
- Both `.json` and `.toml` formats are supported

## Recommendation

To see the correct JSON schema, consult the example files in the repository's `/monitors` folder, as the README defers to those for the specific format specifications.

# =============================================================================
# Monitoring LXC - OpenTelemetry + Prometheus + Grafana + Uptime Kuma + ntfy
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 500
# IP: 192.168.1.229
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Observability stack for metrics, dashboards, and alerting.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 500
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 4096
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 32
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "monitoring" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "monitoring"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.monitoring}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 1024

  rootfs_storage = "tank"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Privileged for Docker
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Monitoring"
  service_description = "OpenTelemetry-based monitoring stack with Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting"

  service_urls = {
    grafana      = "https://grafana.${var.domain_internal}"
    prometheus   = "https://prometheus.${var.domain_internal}"
    alertmanager = "https://alertmanager.${var.domain_internal}"
    uptime_kuma  = "https://status.${var.domain_internal}"

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # OpenTelemetry Collector - Central telemetry receiver and router
  # ==========================================================================
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:latest
    container_name: otel-collector
    command: ["--config=/etc/otelcol/config.yaml"]
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # OTLP gRPC receiver
      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP receiver
      - "8888:8888"   # Prometheus metrics (collector self-metrics)
      - "8889:8889"   # Prometheus exporter (for scraped metrics)
    volumes:
      - ./otel-collector/config.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml:ro
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prometheus - Metrics storage and alerting
  # ==========================================================================
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:latest
    container_name: prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d'
      - '--web.enable-lifecycle'
      - '--web.enable-remote-write-receiver'
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./prometheus/alerts:/etc/prometheus/alerts:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Alertmanager - Alert routing and notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:latest
    container_name: alertmanager
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml'
      - '--storage.path=/alertmanager'
    ports:
      - "9093:9093"
    volumes:
      - ./alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:ro
      - ./alertmanager/templates:/etc/alertmanager/templates:ro
      - alertmanager_data:/alertmanager
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:

  # ==========================================================================

    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:latest

# =============================================================================
# Traefik LXC - Reverse Proxy & Ingress Controller
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 200
# IP: 192.168.1.235
#
# This deployment uses the docker-lxc module which handles:
#   1. LXC container creation with Docker pre-installed
#   2. File sync via rsync (file-sync module)
#   3. Docker Compose deployment
#   4. Proxmox notes generation
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# App-specific Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  description = "Container ID for Traefik LXC"
  type        = number
  default     = 200
}

variable "cores" {
  description = "CPU cores"
  type        = number
  default     = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  description = "Memory in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 2048
}

variable "swap" {
  description = "Swap in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 1024
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  description = "Root filesystem size in GB"
  type        = number
  default     = 8
}

variable "rootfs_storage" {
  description = "Storage pool for root filesystem"
  type        = string
  default     = "nvme-containers"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "traefik" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "traefik"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (dual-NIC: container network + LAN for external access)
  container_ip = "${local.traefik_ip}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.traefik}${local.network.lan_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = var.rootfs_storage
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # MUST be privileged for binding to ports 80/443
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude migrated routes (managed by traefik-route module) and env templates (env is generated)
  exclude_patterns = ["^migrated-dynamic/", "^\\.env"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Traefik"
  service_description = "Reverse proxy and ingress controller for all homelab services"

  service_urls = {
    dashboard_internal = "https://traefik.${var.domain_internal}/dashboard/"
    direct             = "http://${local.traefik_ip}:8080/dashboard/"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "HTTP", port = 80, info = "HTTP entrypoint (redirects to HTTPS)" },
    { name = "HTTPS", port = 443, info = "HTTPS entrypoint with Let's Encrypt" },
    { name = "Metrics", port = 8082, info = "Prometheus metrics endpoint" },
    { name = "Portainer Agent", port = 9001, info = "Container management agent" }
  ]

  custom_notes = file("${path.module}/notes.md")

  tags = ["traefik", "ingress", "reverse-proxy"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets from 1Password, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "traefik_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    cf_api_token = local.op.cloudflare_api_token
    cf_api_email = "darshanrambhia@live.com"
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/traefik.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "traefik_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.traefik_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = local.traefik_ip

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.traefik]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.traefik.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.traefik.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.traefik.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    dashboard_internal = "https://traefik.${var.domain_internal}/dashboard/"
  }
}

# =============================================================================
# Jellyfin LXC - Media Server
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 401
# IP: 192.168.1.226

module "jellyfin" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "jellyfin"
  container_id = 401
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (dual-NIC: container network + LAN for DLNA/casting)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.media.jellyfin}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.jellyfin}${local.network.lan_netmask}"

  cores  = 4
  memory = 8192
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = 32

  unprivileged = false

  # Note: Mount point for /data/library must be added manually via Proxmox SSH
  # The API token doesn't have permission to add bind mounts (requires root@pam)
  # Run this after container creation:
  # ssh root@homelab "pct set 401 -mp0 /tank/data/library,mp=/data/library"
  mount_points = []

  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  service_name        = "Jellyfin"
  service_description = "Media server for movies, TV shows, and music"

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://jellyfin.${var.domain_internal}"
    public   = "https://jellyfin.${var.domain_public}"
    direct   = "http://192.168.1.226:8096"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Jellyfin", port = 8096, info = "Media server UI" },
    { name = "Portainer Agent", port = 9001, info = "Container management agent" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Quick Commands
**View logs:** cd /config && docker compose logs -f jellyfin
**Restart:** cd /config && docker compose restart jellyfin
EOT

  tags = ["jellyfin", "media"]
}

module "jellyfin_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "jellyfin"
  backend_url = "http://${module.jellyfin.ip_address}:8096"

  internal_domain = "jellyfin.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "jellyfin.${var.domain_public}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.jellyfin]
}

# Jellystat - Jellyfin statistics dashboard
module "jellystat_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "jellystat"
  backend_url = "http://${module.jellyfin.ip_address}:3000"

  internal_domain = "jellystat.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Requires Authelia authentication
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authelia", "internal-only"]

  depends_on = [module.jellyfin]
}

# Jellyseerr/Requests - Media request management
module "requests_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "requests"
  backend_url = "http://${module.jellyfin.ip_address}:5055"

  internal_domain = "requests.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "requests.${var.domain_public}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["public-security"]

  depends_on = [module.jellyfin]
}

output "container_id" { value = module.jellyfin.container_id }
output "ip_address" { value = module.jellyfin.ip_address }
output "ssh_command" { value = module.jellyfin.ssh_command }
output "urls" {
  value = {
    jellyfin  = { internal = module.jellyfin_route.internal_url, public = module.jellyfin_route.public_url }
    jellystat = { internal = module.jellystat_route.internal_url }
    requests  = { internal = module.requests_route.internal_url, public = module.requests_route.public_url }
  }
}

# =============================================================================
# Traefik LXC - Reverse Proxy & Ingress Controller
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 200
# IP: 192.168.1.235
#
# This deployment uses the docker-lxc module which handles:
#   1. LXC container creation with Docker pre-installed
#   2. File sync via rsync (file-sync module)
#   3. Docker Compose deployment
#   4. Proxmox notes generation
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# App-specific Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  description = "Container ID for Traefik LXC"
  type        = number
  default     = 200
}

variable "cores" {
  description = "CPU cores"
  type        = number
  default     = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  description = "Memory in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 2048
}

variable "swap" {
  description = "Swap in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 1024
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  description = "Root filesystem size in GB"
  type        = number
  default     = 8
}

variable "rootfs_storage" {
  description = "Storage pool for root filesystem"
  type        = string
  default     = "nvme-containers"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "traefik" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "traefik"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (dual-NIC: container network + LAN for external access)
  container_ip = "${local.traefik_ip}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.traefik}${local.network.lan_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = var.rootfs_storage
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # MUST be privileged for binding to ports 80/443
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude migrated routes (managed by traefik-route module) and env templates (env is generated)
  exclude_patterns = ["^migrated-dynamic/", "^\\.env"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Traefik"
  service_description = "Reverse proxy and ingress controller for all homelab services"

  service_urls = {
    dashboard_internal = "https://traefik.${var.domain_internal}/dashboard/"
    direct             = "http://${local.traefik_ip}:8080/dashboard/"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "HTTP", port = 80, info = "HTTP entrypoint (redirects to HTTPS)" },
    { name = "HTTPS", port = 443, info = "HTTPS entrypoint with Let's Encrypt" },
    { name = "Metrics", port = 8082, info = "Prometheus metrics endpoint" },
    { name = "Portainer Agent", port = 9001, info = "Container management agent" }
  ]

  custom_notes = file("${path.module}/notes.md")

  tags = ["traefik", "ingress", "reverse-proxy"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets from 1Password, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "traefik_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    cf_api_token = local.op.cloudflare_api_token
    cf_api_email = "darshanrambhia@live.com"
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/traefik.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "traefik_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.traefik_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = local.traefik_ip

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.traefik]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.traefik.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.traefik.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.traefik.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    dashboard_internal = "https://traefik.${var.domain_internal}/dashboard/"
  }
}
